content.title: About
content.content: Toasted challah is a traditional Jewish bread made from a yeasted dough, often served with egg. Toasting creates a crisp crust while the crumb stays soft and aromatic. It is commonly used for breakfasts, sandwiches, and as a base for egg dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Challah is braided, symbolizing unity and continuity.
Egg is traditionally added to the dough, giving it a golden hue and subtle richness.
Toasting enhances caramelization, producing a crunchy crust.
In Jewish culture challah is served on Shabbat and holidays.
Variants include raisins, poppy seeds, sesame, or plain.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The bread provides sustained energy through slow-release glucose.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B3 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Egg in the dough adds complete animal protein, aiding tissue repair.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Challah supplies iron, magnesium and phosphorus, important for bones and blood formation.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions support digestion and satiety.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional challah contains wheat, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Toasting and the added egg make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes include salt; individuals with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted challah can be served with butter, avocado, cheese, smoked salmon, or used as a base for sandwiches with egg, vegetables and spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep toasted challah in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag and reheat in the oven before serving.

chicken-or-turkey-and-potatoes-with-grav.title: Chicken or turkey and potatoes with gravy

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of roasted or braised chicken or turkey meat served with boiled or baked potatoes and a gravy made from meat broth, cream or flour. It is a traditional hearty meal popular at family lunches and holiday tables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey belong to the pheasant family, but their meat differs in flavor and fat content.
Traditionally the potatoes are cooked with the skin on to retain nutrients.
Gravy is often made from the pan drippings left after cooking the meat, enhancing the aroma.
Some regions add herbs (rosemary, thyme) or spices (paprika) to the gravy for extra flavor.
The dish can be adapted for dietary needs by using lean cuts or dairy‑free alternatives in the sauce.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium and magnesium, helping maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared without excess oil, the dish is low in saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Serving potatoes with the skin adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to proteins in chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravy often contains salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: High glycemic index of potatoes
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, which can quickly raise blood sugar in diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the meat into portions and placing potatoes alongside. Pour gravy over the meat or serve it on the side. Fresh vegetables or herbs can be added for extra balance.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat thoroughly to a boil to destroy any bacteria. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months, preferably divided into single servings.

coffee-mocha-instant-pre-lightened-and-p.title: Instant Mocha Coffee, Pre‑lightened and Pre‑sweetened with Low‑Calorie Sweetener, Reconstituted (5210)

content.title: About
content.content: Instant mocha coffee is a soluble coffee blended with cocoa powder, pre‑lightened and pre‑sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener. It dissolves quickly in hot water, delivering a fragrant drink with chocolate notes and a gentle sweetness without extra calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mocha combines coffee and cocoa flavors, making it popular among sweet‑drink lovers.
Pre‑lightening speeds up dissolution and reduces bitterness.
Low‑calorie sweeteners (e.g., stevia) lower the energy value while preserving sweetness.
Soluble coffee retains most of the antioxidants found in freshly brewed coffee.
Portion‑packaged sachets provide convenience and easy portion control.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine enhances alertness, improves concentration, and can increase metabolic rate.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The use of a low‑calorie sweetener keeps the drink’s calorie count minimal, suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Mood support
items.content: Caffeine and cocoa aroma can improve mood and reduce feelings of fatigue.

items.title: Convenient consumption
items.content: The instant format allows quick preparation anywhere without a coffee machine.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat with excessive caffeine intake.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: People allergic to cocoa or other ingredients should avoid this product.

items.title: Sweetener tolerance
items.content: Certain low‑calorie sweeteners can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in large amounts.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of some medications, such as central nervous system stimulants.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Pour 200 ml of hot (not boiling) water into a cup, add one sachet (≈2 g) of instant mocha coffee, stir thoroughly until fully dissolved. Optionally add milk or cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep sachets in a dry, cool place, protected from moisture and direct sunlight. After opening, use within 3–6 months.

corn-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked-with-o.title: Corn, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Canned corn with reduced sodium is cooked in oil, giving it a tender texture and a mild buttery flavor. The product is shelf‑stable and ready to eat straight from the can.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the most widely cultivated vegetables, grown in over 100 countries.
Canning preserves most B‑vitamins and carotenoids.
Reduced sodium makes the product more suitable for people watching their salt intake.
Cooking in oil enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Corn provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Low sodium combined with healthy fats helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Provides magnesium
items.content: Magnesium is essential for normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn.

items.title: Oil content
items.content: The product contains added oil, which may be undesirable on very low‑fat diets.

items.title: Damaged cans
items.content: If the can lid is dented or bulging, discard it due to possible bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the corn straight from the can, add it to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, or use it as a filling for wraps. It can also be quickly warmed in a skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep the corn in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑4 days.

content.title: About
content.content: French or Catalina Light Dressing is a flavorful sauce made from vegetable oils, vinegar, spices, and a touch of sugar. It is intended for dressing salads, vegetable dishes, and seafood, giving them a light sweet‑tart note without excess calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend combines classic French herbs with the mild sweetness typical of Catalina dressing.
The light version contains less fat and fewer calories than traditional dressings, thanks to reduced‑fat oil and vinegar.
Common ingredients include Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and aromatic herbs such as basil, oregano, and parsley.
It fits well into low‑carb and weight‑management diets.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Provides flavor without significantly increasing the energy value of a dish.

items.title: Source of plant oils
items.content: Olive and sunflower oils supply monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and spices (basil, oregano) contain vitamin K, vitamin C, and polyphenols that help protect cells.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar and lemon juice stimulate gastric juice production, aiding nutrient absorption.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: Minimal added sugar makes it suitable for people monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: May contain mustard, egg, or dairy components—check the label if you have allergies.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some formulations have higher salt levels; individuals with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Vinegar and lemon can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drizzle over ready salads, raw vegetables, boiled chicken, or seafood. It can also be mixed into marinades for grilling or used as a sandwich spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated after opening in a tightly sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 4–6 weeks. Discard if the smell or taste changes.

content.title: About
content.content: Moo Goo Gai Pan is a classic Chinese dish made with chicken breast, shiitake mushrooms, and vegetables, cooked in a light soy‑ginger‑garlic sauce. It has a delicate, mildly salty and slightly sweet flavor and is often served over rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Moo Goo Gai Pan” means “chicken with mushrooms” in Cantonese.
The dish originated in Canton in the early 20th century and quickly spread to Chinese restaurants worldwide.
Traditionally it uses skinless chicken breast, making it a relatively low‑fat option.
Shiitake mushrooms add a strong umami taste and are rich in B‑vitamins.
Original recipes sometimes include toasted cashews or almonds for added crunch.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides a high‑quality source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skinless chicken and minimal oil keep the dish low in total fat, suitable for lean‑diet plans.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shiitake mushrooms contain niacin, riboflavin, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Shiitake mushrooms are rich in polysaccharides (lentinan) and ergothioneine, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans in mushrooms may help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Allergy to chicken or mushrooms
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat or shiitake mushrooms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds a notable amount of salt; those monitoring sodium should use low‑sodium soy sauce.

items.title: MSG presence
items.content: The dish may contain monosodium glutamate, which can cause headaches or flushing in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Moo Goo Gai Pan is served hot, typically alongside steamed rice or noodles. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. For extra heat, add a dash of chili sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave, adding a splash of water to retain moisture.

orange-juice-100-with-calcium-added-froz.title: Orange juice, 100%, with calcium added, frozen, reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: Orange juice, 100%, with calcium added is a frozen concentrate that, once reconstituted, provides a fully natural juice with enhanced calcium content. The juice is made from ripe oranges and undergoes rapid freezing, preserving vitamin C and other nutrients. Calcium is added in a soluble form that fully dissolves during reconstitution.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezing for a few minutes retains over 90% of vitamin C compared with traditional pasteurised juice.
Calcium is added as micro‑crystalline particles that dissolve completely when water is added.
Reconstituted juice tastes and smells like fresh‑pressed juice but can be stored longer without quality loss.
Orange juice is one of the world’s most popular beverages, with more than 70 million tonnes consumed annually.
The drink is often used in sports nutrition because of its vitamin C and calcium combination.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Added calcium strengthens bones and teeth, especially important for children, adolescents and older adults.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The juice contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for cell division and especially beneficial during pregnancy.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Being mostly water, the juice helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oranges.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural sugars may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of the juice can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Vitamin C can affect the efficacy of certain drugs, such as anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, sauces and marinades. To reconstitute the frozen concentrate, add the specified amount of cold water, stir well and chill before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen concentrate at –18 °C or lower. After reconstitution, store in the refrigerator for no more than 3–4 days. Do not leave the juice at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

pizza-with-meat-other-than-pepperoni-stu.title: Pizza with meat and stuffed crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with meat (excluding pepperoni) and a stuffed crust is a classic Italian dish where a thin dough base is topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and a variety of meats such as ham, chicken, beef, or sausage. The stuffed crust contains an inner layer of cheese, making it especially flavorful and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Neapolitan pizza is baked in a wood‑fired oven at about 485 °C for 60–90 seconds.
Stuffed crust was introduced in the United States in the 1990s as a way to add extra cheesy goodness.
Meat toppings often include smoked ham, chicken breast, or ground beef, but never pepperoni in this variation.
There are more than 30 dough styles for pizza, ranging from thin “Neapolitan” to thicker “Chicago” style.
In Italy, pizza is often served with minimal toppings to let the dough and sauce shine.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella cheese supplies calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain crust deliver vitamins B6 and B12, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The combination of carbs, fats, and protein provides lasting satiety and energy.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Meat‑topped pizza with a cheese‑filled crust can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and meat contain saturated fats, which can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meats often contain a lot of salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should choose alternative cheeses.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pizza hot, sliced into individual portions. Fresh herbs (basil, oregano) or a light green salad make a nice accompaniment. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain dough and reduce the amount of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crispy.

turkey-light-and-dark-meat-roasted-skin-.title: Turkey, light and dark meat, roasted, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a large poultry bird raised mainly for its meat. Light meat (breast) is lower in fat and calories, while dark meat (thighs, drumsticks) is richer, juicier, and more flavorful. Roasted meat without skin retains most nutrients and works well in a variety of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is a national symbol in the United States, especially on Thanksgiving.
Light meat contains about 30 % fewer calories than dark meat.
Dark meat is higher in iron and zinc compared with breast meat.
Roasting without skin reduces saturated fat while preserving flavor through natural juices.
Turkey belongs to the pheasant family and is closely related to chickens.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Turkey meat provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat in breast meat
items.content: Skin‑less breast meat is very low in saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey is rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Dark meat especially supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Very low carbohydrate
items.content: Turkey contains virtually no carbs, fitting well into low‑carb eating plans.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey meat.

items.title: Handling and storage
items.content: Improper storage of roasted turkey can allow bacterial growth leading to foodborne illness.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: If the turkey is seasoned with salt or sauces, sodium levels can become high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted, skin‑less turkey can be sliced for salads, sandwiches, pastas, or used as a base for soups. Breast strips work well for quick meals, while dark meat adds heartiness to stews and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep roasted turkey in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it retains quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
